note: Evil Mode slice 12, the fires (design Part 19; Part 30 section 7 `fires`). Once a region the Boss can sit across a camp-fire from the Hero, out of uniform; the Hero doesn't know who they're talking to. Three exchanges, then one thing of the player's own, kept whole and quoted back in the last room. Every choice is a question or silence (listening) or a statement (talking); the screen doesn't say which. Slots in braces are read from the run; each has a written fallback. Text is data; the save keeps ids and the player's own words. Numbers are starting values; none are playtested.

flame.board: A small flame at step {step}. The Hero's resting.
flame.why: Takes the day's in-person slot. That Night nobody knocks.
flame.gone: There was a fire on the road a night ago. It's out.
flame.missed: Thought somebody might turn up. There's usually somebody on this road. Nobody did.
flame.pastTalking: They don't make camp. They walk through the night.
flame.had: Sat at a fire with {name}. They don't know who you are.
flame.night: Nobody knocks. The Boss sits alone. There's a notebook on the Office desk.
flame.noteNone: Not tonight. The notebook's for the night after a fire.

scene.title: A fire
scene.set: A fire. Somebody on the other side of it, with a {mon} asleep on their feet.
scene.setAwake: A fire. Somebody on the other side of it. Their {mon}'s awake, and watching you.
scene.own: Then: one thing of your own.
scene.ownHelp: Type it (up to 120 letters), or pick one. It's kept, word for word.
scene.end: The fire burns down. In the morning they're gone up the road.

andYou.ask: "What about you? What're you doing all the way out here?"

reply: They nod. "That sounds hard."
"My mum says that when she doesn't want to say."
They let it go. They remember that they let it go.
They believe it. "Is it all right? Working there?"
"Is it a good one?"

cause.say: "There's something that's wrong and I'm trying to put it right."
reply: "Me too!" A pause. "...It's probably not the same thing."

power.say: "Finding out how far I can get."
reply: "Me too." No pause. They like you at once.
"What'll you do when you find it?"

belonging.say: "I've a lot of people waiting for me to come back."
reply: They look at the fire. "That must be nice."
"Me too." This time they look up.
"Good." They don't sound sure it's good.
"Then why d'you stay?" They don't wait for an answer. They think they know it.

answers.say: "I've been on this road a long time."
reply: They accept it.
Their eyes narrow.
They get up. They don't run. They stand on the far side of the fire with their {mon} awake in front of them.
The whole truth. They hear it out to the end.
The last fire won't happen now. This was it.

slots.ledgerNone: It's all the same. That's what's odd. Nobody's all the same.
slots.personLineNone: She said she won't do the bad jobs. Why's she in it?

open: "There's a team round here. {reason} I'm going to find whoever's in charge. I don't know what I'll do. I've only got a {mon}."

reply: "I've been practising. 'Give it back.' That's as far as I've got. ...It's not very good, is it. I thought if I got there I'd know the rest."
A long look at the fire. "Maybe. I can't think of a reason that'd be good enough. But I'd want to hear it. I think I'd want to hear it more than I'd want it back."
A Potion. They take it. They use it at once, on the {mon}, before saying thank you.
"...Thanks. Sorry. He comes first. You'd be the same."
ex1.file: A stranger fixed his foot. Didn't want anything.

first.ask: "Can I ask you something? You've got strong Pokémon. D'you ever *not* fight when you could? When you'd win?"

reply: "Good. I thought it was just me being scared."
They look up. "...That's honest."
"There was one of them at a door. She was shaking. I could've won. I gave her a Berry and went round. I keep thinking I should've fought."

open: "It's you again. You're always on this road." They've a second Pokémon now, asleep against the first.
"I found out more. Somebody mended what they broke. My uncle says the team did it. I don't— can you make that make sense?"

reply: "No. Me neither. I'm glad it's not just me."

ex1.say: "Maybe it's two different people giving the orders."
reply: "I thought that. Then I met one who'd done both. She couldn't explain it either. She said, 'Ask the Boss.'"
A while. "...I think it does. For me. I can't go home and say 'they're bad except when they're not.' My mum'll say 'Well, which?'"

second.ask: "When you were my age. Did anyone ever tell you the truth about something big?"

reply: "Was it worse than not knowing?" They don't wait. "Don't say. I'll find out."
"Yeah." They poke the fire. "That's what I'm doing."

ex3.say: "What would you want to be told?"
reply: "Whether the people who did it are sorry. That's all. I could carry the rest."

open: "You know a lot about them. You always know where they've been." They aren't accusing. They've put a tin on to boil, for two.
"I'm not going to ask. I think if I ask you'll have to lie or I'll have to do something. I don't want either tonight."
third.told: "I know. I've known since the boat. I wanted one more fire first."

reply: "Don't. It's not for you. It's for me." They pour the tea anyway. Two cups.
It's too sweet. They watch you drink it and nod, as if that settled something.

ex1.say: "What would you do, if you asked?"
reply: "I don't know. That's why I'm not asking."

third.ask: "If somebody's done bad things for a good reason. Do you still have to stop them?"

reply: "Yeah. I thought you'd say that. I hoped you wouldn't."
"The people in my street. That's who's paying."
"I think you stop them. And then you listen. In that order."

open: "I'm coming tomorrow. To the building. You know that."

"I'm not going to say anything clever. I'm going to walk in and look at everything and then I'm going to ask you one thing. So. Think about your answer. Please. I've come a long way and I'd like it to be a good one."

reply: "Good."
"You know what it is."
They nod back. It's the most they've agreed on.

last.ask: "Is there anything you'd want me to see? Before I ask?"

reply: "Okay. I'll look at the kitchen."
"That's what I was going to do."
"People. That's what I keep forgetting. It's people."

open: "Eight Badges. That's all I want. There's some gang keeps putting people at doors. It's *slow.*"

reply: "The League. Then Champion." A pause. "...Then I don't know. Nobody asks that. Then I'm Champion, I s'pose, for ever." They poke the fire. "That's a long time."
"Then I'd beat whoever they put in them. A Badge is a Badge." Then, slower: "...Is it? If somebody's paid for the Leader to lose. Is that a Badge?"
ex1.file: Will check every Gym from now on. "If it's too easy I'm asking why."

reply: "Because there's three others started the same day and one of them's better than me." A beat. "I didn't say that. Forget I said that."

first.ask: "You've done all this, right? Badges and that. Was it worth it?"

reply: "Good." Relieved. Not convinced.

ex3.say: "It wasn't the Badges that were worth it."
reply: "Everyone old says that." They think about it for the rest of the region.
They stare. "Why *not?*"
ex3.file: Met someone who didn't finish. They seemed all right.

open: "It's you again. You're always on this road." They're not sitting. They're stretching.
"I've got five. The gang had two of the Gyms. One of them, they'd put their own person in. She was *good.* It was the best fight I've had. I don't know how I feel about that."

reply: "Angry. It'd be simpler."
"That's what she said! After. She shook my hand. She had the armband on and she shook my hand."
They take it out. "It's got their mark on. I'm going to have to explain that at the League." They put it back with the others. In order.

second.ask: "D'you think the League'll count it? A Badge off one of theirs?"

reply: "Yeah. Yeah, it is." They sound like they're telling themselves.
"...It matters to me. That's annoying."
"I'm not asking *them* anything. I'm beating them."

open: "You know a lot about them." Flat.
"I don't care who you are. I mean that nicely. I've got seven and there's one left and they're between me and it. If you're with them, tell them to put somebody good on the door."
third.told: "Yeah. I worked that out a while ago. Doesn't change the door."

reply: "Good." Then, almost a smile: "Somebody *really* good."
"Because if it's easy it doesn't count. I've had enough that didn't count."
They take that as a yes. They're probably right.

third.ask: "What do you do, after? When the thing you wanted's done?"

reply: "That's what I was afraid of."
They laugh. It's real. "I don't know how."

ex3.say: "What do you want it to be?"
reply: "...I don't know. I've never got that far. I've always been chasing."

open: "Eight." They hold them up to the firelight, fanned, like cards.
"It was meant to feel like something. It feels like I've got a thing to do tomorrow first. That's your fault. I wanted you to know I know that."

reply: "Good. As long as we both know."

ex1.say: "What do you want it to feel like?"
reply: "Finished."
They let you. They don't put them away till you've looked at each one.

last.ask: "If I win tomorrow. Will you still be on this road?"

reply: "Huh. Okay."
They don't answer. They don't say no.
"Everyone's said that. All eight of them."

open: "I've been writing down what they do. Look. {kind} {worst} It's the same people. I can't make it one thing."
openNo: "I've been writing down what they do. Look." {ledger}

reply: "Then it's two things with one name on, and that's worse, because which one answers when I knock?" They write that down.
"The worst one. People are what they do when it costs them nothing to be worse." A pause. "...But the good one cost them something. I priced it. So that isn't it either."
They've priced it. The figure's low: they don't know what labour costs.
They hand it over.

first.ask: "If you wanted to know what somebody was *for.* Not what they said. How'd you find out?"

ex3.say: "Watch what they do when nobody's looking."
reply: "I've been trying. They always seem to know when I'm looking."

ex3.say: "Ask the people who work for them."
reply: "I did. I got eleven different answers. I wrote them all down. One of them said 'dental.'"
They stop writing. "...Just ask. Walk in and ask." They underline something.

open: "It's you again. You're always on this road." The notebook's a second notebook now.
"I've worked something out. They never take from the same person twice. Either that's a rule or it's a coincidence, and I don't believe in coincidences."

reply: "Then somebody made it. Somebody sat down and decided. I want to meet that person."
"Then I cross out four pages. I've done it before." They show you. They have.
Two columns. Every name. A tick against each, once. They're right.
They look at you for a long moment. "...So do they."
"Do you read them?" "Every week." "Good."
"Because I can't make theirs add up and I think it's because there's a column I can't see."

open: "You know a lot about them." They've turned to a page near the front.
"First fire: you said, '{own}' I wrote it down. It's the only thing anyone's said to me that I couldn't file under anything. I've got a page that's just that."
openNo: "You know a lot about them." They've turned to a page near the front.
"First fire, you didn't say anything. You put a log on. I wrote that down too. It's the only blank page in the book."
third.told: "I know. I had it in the second column for two regions. I just hadn't underlined it."

reply: "Because it doesn't fit. Things that don't fit are where the answer is."
"I know. That's why it's got its own page."
Your words, in a child's careful hand. Underlined twice.

third.ask: "What's the column I can't see? You know. I can tell you know."

reply: They write the word at the top of a fresh page. Nothing under it yet.
"Who it's for." They write it down. "That's going to take a region."
"That's the problem. I'd have to ask them. Every line."

open: "I've finished the notebook. There's two columns and I've added them up. D'you want to know which is longer?"
They don't say. They put the notebook on the ground between the two of you, closed, and leave it there when they go to bed.

reply: It's the Ledger's last page, a day early, in their hand. The totals are wrong in the team's favour: they still don't know what labour costs.
It's still there in the morning. So are they. "You didn't read it." "No." "Huh."
"Do you," they say, from inside the tent. It isn't a question.

last.ask: "Tomorrow I'm going to ask you to fill in the second column. Will you?"

reply: "Bring a pen. I've only got the one."
"Some's more than anyone else has."
"Then I'll know. That's the whole point of a book."

open: "One of them beat me. {grunt}. Fair. I've not stopped thinking about it. Afterwards he gave me a *sandwich.*"
openNo: "I've beaten all of them that stood in front of me. Not one's said who's in charge. They just shrug. I want to hit something that knows why it's being hit."

reply: Thrown. "...Cheese. And something. Pickle. Why does that matter?" A pause. "It was good. That's what's annoying."

ex1.say: "Did you want to beat him or be him?"
reply: They're on their feet. "I—" They sit down again. "He wasn't angry. He won and he wasn't angry and he made a sandwich. I've never won and not been angry."
They are. They sit. "...Nobody tells me to sit down. They tell me to calm down. It's not the same."

first.ask: "How d'you stop being angry at somebody who's been decent to you?"

reply: "Then what do I do with it?"
Nothing, for a while. "...There was a kid at school. It doesn't matter."

ex3.say: "Go and ask him for another sandwich."
reply: A bark of a laugh. The first. "I might."

open: "It's you again. You're always on this road." They don't look pleased. They've made room on the log anyway.
"I beat him. The sandwich one. Second go. He said 'Good. You'd been leaving your left side open.' He *coached* me. After *losing.* What is *wrong* with these people?"

reply: "That's worse. That's so much worse."

ex1.say: "Were you leaving your left side open?"
reply: A long silence. "...Yes."
"No." A pause. "I'm going to have to, aren't I."

second.ask: "Is it stupid to want to fight the one in charge just to see if they're like him?"

reply: "Good. Because I'm going to."
"Then I'll know what to do with the anger."
They don't answer that one. They put another log on, too hard.

open: "You know a lot about them. Don't. Don't say anything. If you're one of them I'll have to fight you and I'm *tired.*"
A long while.
"...Are they all right? The ones I've beaten. Do they get in trouble?"
third.told: "Yeah. I know. I've known since the sandwich. Nobody else'd make one."

reply: "Good. I didn't— good."
"Which ones? ...No. Don't tell me. Tell whoever's in charge that if they dock the sandwich one I'll burn the place down." They mean it about one-third.
"Because I beat them. It's not their fault I beat them."

third.ask: "When you were angry, at my age. What did you do with it?"

reply: They look at you for a long time. "...Yeah. I can see that."
"Honest."

ex3.say: "What do you want to do with yours?"
reply: "Put it somewhere it'll do some good. I just don't know where that is."

open: "I'm going to walk in there tomorrow and I'm going to be *so* angry. I've been saving it."
"I want you to know it's not about you. I mean it is. But it's not *only.*"

reply: "Good."
"Everyone who ever made me sit in the corridor."
A short laugh. "There'll be loads left. There always is."

last.ask: "If I lose tomorrow. Will they still feed me?"

reply: "Okay." They lie down. They're asleep almost at once.
They don't answer. They don't stop smiling either.
"Because I'm *tired.* I've been tired since the first region."

open: "I met one! One of the team! {person}! They're *nice.* {personLine} Why are they in it?"

reply: "I did! They said 'It's a long story and you've got a Badge to get.' So I said I've got time and they said 'I haven't.' But they smiled."
"Everybody goes! You get your first one and you go. I didn't think about it. ...Should I have thought about it?"

ex1.say: "Maybe it's the only place that'd have them."
reply: They stop smiling. "That's sad. That's really sad. Is that true? ...I'm going to ask them that."

first.ask: "D'you think people are mostly good? I do. Everyone says I'll grow out of it."

reply: Delighted. "I won't!"
"When does it count?"

ex3.say: "What'd you do if you met one who wasn't?"
reply: "...I don't know. I've been trying to. I keep meeting your— I keep meeting *their* people and they keep being all right."

open: "It's you again! You're always on this road! Sit, sit. I've got loads to tell you."
They've a list. It's names, each with a note. "I'm trying to meet all of them. Then I'll know."

reply: They do. "Funny." "Scary then not." "SOUP." Every one of them's somebody you know.
"Whether it's a bad thing with good people in, or a good thing with bad people in. It's got to be one."
"Of them? They're *lovely.*" A pause. "Mostly."

second.ask: "Is it rude to ask somebody if they're happy?"

reply: "Me. I'm asking." They grin.
"Good. Because I've been asking everybody."
"Mostly 'fine.' One of them didn't say anything. I sat with him for a bit."

open: "You know a lot about them." Cheerfully.
"You're one of them, aren't you. It's fine! I've met loads. You're the oldest, though. Are you a— what's the one above Lead?"
third.told: The cheer goes out of them like a breath. Then: "...Oh. Oh, that's— okay. Okay. Then I've got a lot of questions and you have to answer all of them because I've been *really nice* about this."

reply: "I *knew* it." They're thrilled. They've got it wrong, and you can see they don't think so.
"You talk about them like you know where they keep the spoons."
They smile back. They take it as a yes to whatever they thought.
"That's what everyone says. It's always 'some days.'"
They go quiet. They sit closer. They don't say anything for the rest of the fire.
"Yes! Mostly. Except about this."

open: "I've met {met} of them. Most were nice. Some were sad. One was horrible."
"So tomorrow I'm coming to find out which sort you are. I'm hoping. I want you to know I'm hoping."

reply: They tell you. You know the name.
"I always do. It's the one thing I'm good at."
"I don't know! That's why I'm *coming.*"

last.ask: "Will they all be there? Tomorrow? I want to say goodbye properly."

reply: "Good. I've brought sweets."
They look up, very fast.
"Because after tomorrow it's different. Whatever happens."

open: "They've got a sentence. On their door. I read it." They say it: "'{sentence}'"
"I've been thinking about it for three days. I don't think it's wrong. I think they're not doing it."

reply: At once, as if they'd been waiting for someone to ask: "{doing}"
"No they're not. I've tried to write one. For me. For what I'm for. I've crossed out eleven." They show the page. "They got theirs down to one line. That's hard. I just want them to *mean* it."

ex1.say: "Why d'you care if they mean it?"
reply: "Because if they do, I'm fighting the wrong people." A pause. "And if they don't, somebody should tell them what it says."

first.ask: "Have you ever said you'd do a thing, and then done a smaller thing, and told yourself it was the same?"

reply: They nod, slowly. "What did you do after?" You tell them you're still deciding. They accept that.
"That's not an answer. That's a place to hide." Not unkindly.
"...I told my mum I was going for Badges. I'm not. I've got three and I haven't looked at them. I'm going for the door with the sentence on."

open: "It's you again. You're always on this road." They've the sentence written on their hand, in ink, half washed off.
{changed}

reply: "I hope so. I really hope so."
"The door. Nobody should need a man on a door."
"So I don't forget what I'm holding them to."

second.ask: "Do you think a group can mean something? Or only people?"

reply: "Then I'll need to find the person."

ex3.say: "A group can, if it's small enough."
reply: "How small?" They look at you as if you'd know.
"I think a group means whatever the worst person in it'll do."

open: "You know a lot about them. You talk about them like— like they're yours to be disappointed in."
They've got it. They don't say so.
third.told: "I know. I think I've known since the sentence. It sounded like you."

reply: "Then do something about it. You can, can't you."
"The way you say 'them.' It's the way my mum says 'us.'"
They let you. That's an answer too.

third.ask: "If I could say one thing to whoever wrote that sentence. Just one. What should it be?"

reply: "Okay. I'll ask."
"I'll tell them. Out loud."

ex3.say: "Tell them it was a good sentence."
reply: "Was. Okay."

open: "I'm going to read it to you tomorrow. Your sentence. Out loud. In your own Office. And then I'm going to ask if it's still true."
"That's all. I'm not even bringing my best team. I don't think it's that kind of thing."

reply: "Then you won't mind me asking."
"Then I'll write a better one on your wall. Under yours."
"No." Gently. "That's not what it's for."

last.ask: "What's yours? Not theirs. Yours. Your sentence."

reply: "Good. Then we'll see."
"Me too." They show you their hand. Eleven crossings-out.
"Because you'll have to say it tomorrow, and I'd like it to be yours."

open: "My father'd know what to do. He'd have a speech. I've been trying to write one."

reply: They stand up to do it. They've a piece of paper. "'Villains of— of this region. I am—' That's my name. '—and I have come to bring you to justice. Lay down your—' I don't know what they've got. '—your things.'" They sit down. "It's rubbish. His weren't rubbish."

ex1.say: "What would you do, if nobody'd know?"
reply: The longest silence of the night. "...Go and look at the sea, I think. I've never just looked at it. We always had somewhere to be."

ex1.say: "What did he do, when it was him?"
reply: "Won. He always just won. There's a photograph. He's holding a cup and he's not smiling." A pause. "I asked him once what it was like. He said, 'It was what was expected.'"

first.ask: "Were you good at this? When you were my age? I'm good at it. Everyone says. I don't know if I *like* it."

reply: "That sounds better."

ex3.say: "Does it matter if you like it?"
reply: "It's meant not to." They don't sound sure.
Nobody's asked. "...Sandile. I like Sandile. They're not strong. I'm not allowed one on the team."

open: "It's you again. You're always on this road." They're sitting differently. Looser.
"I looked at the sea. Somebody said, what would I do if nobody'd know. I looked at it for two hours. I missed a Gym slot. My father rang. I said I'd been training."
"That's the first time I've lied to him. It was *easy.* Is that bad?"

reply: "Yeah." They seem relieved somebody said it.
"Big. Grey. It didn't care who I was." They smile. "I liked that best."
"Yes." No hesitation at all.

second.ask: "Do you ever do what you want instead of what you should?"

reply: "Does it get easier?" "No." "Oh."
"I thought adults just did what they wanted."
"...I'm starting to."

open: "You know a lot about them. I'm expected to do something about that." They don't move. "I'm so tired of what's expected."

"If you are who I think you are, I'm supposed to fight you now. I've decided I'm going to do it tomorrow. In the proper place. Tonight I'd like to just sit. Is that allowed? I'm asking you. You're the only adult I know who doesn't answer for somebody else."
third.told: "Yes. I know. Thank you for saying it yourself. Nobody in my family ever does."

reply: They let out a breath. They sit back. They look about eleven, for once.
"Nobody. That's the strange part. Nobody's here."
They watch it catch. They don't say anything else for a long time, and it's fine.

third.ask: "When you started. Was it what you wanted? Or what was expected?"

reply: "Then you're luckier than him."
"That sounds lonely. And nice."
"I will." They mean it.

open: "I've written the speech. It's good now." They don't read it.
"I'm not going to use it. I'm going to ask you what you wanted. When you started. Before it was what was expected."

reply: "Good. Tell me the true one. I've heard the other kind all my life."
They do. It's good. It's very good. Then they fold it into a boat and put it in the fire.
"To look at the sea. I've done that now. So I need a new one."

last.ask: "Will you be honest tomorrow? Even if it's worse?"

reply: "Thank you."
"That's more than most."
"...Yes. I think I'm going to be honest with everybody for a while. It's going to be very awkward."

open: "Sorry. Is it all right if I sit here? I can go somewhere else. ...Thanks. Sorry."
A while.
"I lost to one of them today. I lose to most people. She said sorry. *She* said sorry to *me.* I didn't know what to do so I said sorry back."

reply: "Eleven. I've won four. I write them down." They show a tally. It's very neat. "My mum says it's the going that counts. She's being nice."
"...He won't let me stop." The {mon}. It's awake. It's watching you. "Every time I say let's go home he walks the other way."
"Sor—" They stop. They laugh, a bit. "Okay."

first.ask: "Does it get easier? Don't say yes if it doesn't."

reply: They write that on the tally sheet, at the top.
"Okay." They don't believe it. They're grateful it was said.
"...Could you show me what I did wrong? She led with a bug thing and I didn't know what to do."

open: "It's you again. You're always on this road." They didn't ask if they could sit.
"I've won nine. I've stopped writing down the losses. I thought about what you said."
"One of the team's people asked me for advice. A Grunt. He'd lost four in a row. I told him what you told me. Is that— was that helping the enemy?"

reply: "Good. He won his next one. He waved."
"...No. He was sad. That's all that mattered."
"That you don't get easier. You get better." They look at you. "Your words."

second.ask: "Can I show you something? I've been practising."

reply: Their {mon} does a thing it couldn't do a region ago. They're trying very hard not to look proud.
"Okay. Tomorrow." They don't seem to mind.
"I know. I want to."

open: "You know a lot about them." Quietly. Carefully.
"I think you're one. I think you might be the main one. I've thought so since the practice. Nobody who wasn't in charge'd have that many good Pokémon and use the worst."
"I'm not scared of you. I want you to know I've checked and I'm not."
third.told: "I know. I've known since the practice. I just wanted to hear you say it."

reply: "Good," they agree. They sound surprised it's true.
"Because you showed me what I was doing wrong. People who are going to hurt you don't do that."
They nod, as if you'd said something.

third.ask: "If I come to the building. Will you fight me properly? Not easy. Properly."

reply: "Thank you." They mean it more than anything they've said.
"I want."
"Because everyone's always let me off. I want to know if I'm actually good."

open: "I've got eight. Me. I counted them twice." They aren't apologising for anything.
"I'm coming tomorrow. I'm probably going to lose. I've lost to nearly everybody at least once and then I've come back. So if I lose tomorrow I want you to know I'm coming back the day after."

reply: "Good." No sorry. Not once.
"...I hadn't thought about that." They think about it now. They smile, slowly.
"I know. That's why I'm coming."

last.ask: "Do you think I'm good now? Honestly?"

reply: They don't say anything. They just hold their {mon} a bit tighter.
"Better's good. Better's what you said."
"...Yeah. I think I do."

middle.open: "D'you want half of this?" They hold out whatever they're eating.

reply: You eat. Nobody says anything. It's good.
"No idea. A woman in the last town gave it me."
They eat it all. They don't mind.
"Me too."
"Home. That's where I'd be."
They nod back.

middle.open: They're asleep when you get there. The fire's still going. You sit anyway.

reply: They wake up enough to see who it is, and go back to sleep.
"Oh. It's you. Good."
In the morning it's gone, and so are they.

middle.open: "I had a letter from home. D'you want to hear it?"

reply: They read it aloud. It's ordinary. It's the best thing you've heard all region.
They fold it up again. "Okay."
"Mostly."
"So have I. Apparently."
"In a fight with one of theirs. Funny, that."
It looks back at you. It remembers you.

middle.open: "I'm not going to ask you anything tonight."

reply: "Good," they agree.
"Because I know most of it now. And the rest I want to hear somewhere else."
Neither of you does.
Two people under one bit of tarp. The fire hisses.
"There's never room. Budge up."
"It likes it. It's weird."
"Good. I miss my bed."
"Because I'm counting. Not down. Just counting."
"That's what my mum says about pudding."

idealistDoing.cause: Nobody frightened. If it's *for* people you can't frighten people to get it.
idealistDoing.power: Somebody in charge who'd step down if they were wrong. I've never seen that.
idealistDoing.wonder: Looking, and leaving it there. You don't have to take a thing to see it.
idealistDoing.belonging: A door that's open. Theirs has a man on it.
idealistDoing.spite: Just the one person, then. Not everyone in the way.

idealistChanged.yes: "They've changed something. Nobody made them. D'you think somebody on the inside *read it?*"
idealistChanged.no: "Two regions. Same sentence. Same everything. I've stopped thinking they've forgotten. I think they know."

profit: "Count what it costs you. Not just the money."
"Get paid for what you're good at."
"Somebody always pays. Try not to make it the small ones."
cause: "Some things are worth getting in trouble for."
"Don't wait for somebody else to fix it."
"The world's not fair. You don't have to be like it."
power: "Don't let anyone tell you how far to go."
"Strong's not the same as right. Be both."
"Nobody gives it to you. You take it."
"Find out what you're for, before someone tells you."
wonder: "Don't take what you find. Just find it."
"Stay curious. It's harder than it sounds."
belonging: "Somebody's always waiting for you to come back."
spite: "Don't let one person decide who you are."
"Anger's a good fire. Don't sleep in it."
"Some people deserve what's coming. Most don't."
"Don't spend your whole life chasing one person."
"Forgive the ones who didn't know better."

clean: "There's always a better way. Look for it."
"Don't hurt anybody you don't have to."
grey: "Sometimes the right thing's the smaller thing."
"Don't believe everything people say about anyone."
"It's never as simple as it looks."

quoted.said: "You sat across a fire from me and said, {own}"
quoted.silence: "You didn't say anything. You put a log on. I've thought about that more than anything anyone's told me."
quoted.none: "Nobody sat with me. Not once. There's usually somebody on that road."

notebook.title: The notebook
notebook.intro: It's the File, from the other side.
notebook.none: A page of headings. Nothing under them yet.
notebook.prices: A list of prices, each a bit under what was paid.
notebook.total: Total: more than they've taken? CHECK.

practice.begin: A practice battle. No stakes: your weakest against their {mon}.
practice.after: They've watched every move. "Oh. *Oh.* That's what I was doing."
practice.mark: One mark toward the Doctrine: you've just trained the Hero to beat the team, on purpose, because a child asked.

loyalty: {name}, that Evening: "A kid asked me if this was the only place that'd have me. I said no. Then I thought about it. I said, it's the only place I'd have."
heroLine: They'll say it to whoever wrote the sentence. In the last room. Word for word.
